rationale: Both halves of the multi-voter question now have complete comparisons. Receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 (exit 0, twenty-six events, no parse loss) resolves the election check: with RestoreCommittedLogs on and the restarted node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, it became leader with reachable_votes 2 against a committed quorum of 3 (comparison 0 violated, witness event index 22, leader_below_committed_quorum true, majority_side_leader true in the same run), while the flag-off control never won (comparison 1 holds at evaluated event index 25). Together with receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 for the configuration loss, the child question is now answered: the stale rebuilt configuration both misdescribes membership and decides an election the committed configuration would refuse. The remaining open item is entry-level divergence, which the registered gap still asks about and which is not claimed. The two config re-checks in this last declaration were redundant and again incomplete because the two multi-voter scenarios emit the same restart event name; they duplicate the already-complete configuration comparison and carry no new claim, so the interpretation rests on the election comparison from this receipt and the configuration comparison from the earlier one.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose rebuilt configuration is a stale, smaller membership can be elected leader with support that is a minority of the committed configuration: isolated together with one committed voter it became leader with two votes while the committed five-voter configuration requires three, and the same restart without the flag could not win on that side.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the restarted node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, with that partner also cut off from the majority side so requestVote's existing-leader guard does not refuse it; observed with a bounded window against a flag-off control.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: Two completed comparisons answer this question, each with its flag-off control. Configuration: receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 15 - the node restarted from a log whose latest configuration is index 14 with five servers came back at configuration index 1 with three servers, the snapshot's bootstrap configuration - with the control holding at evaluated event index 18 (index 14, five servers). Election: receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 22 - the restarted node, isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returned, became leader with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3, and the same run also reports majority_side_leader true, so a leader elected on a minority of the committed configuration coexisted with the majority-side leader - with the control holding at evaluated event index 25 (became_leader false). Source: after restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index, the startup scan at api.go:604-620 starts above the committed configuration entry, so AddVoter's later entry (api.go:994-1005) is never re-read and the node keeps the snapshot's three-server list; quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) then returns two and electSelf (raft.go:1999-2060) asks only that list, so the node's own vote plus one follower meets its stale quorum while the committed configuration needs three. The consequence is safety relevant rather than merely a stale read: a client that applies through this leader receives success for an entry that lacks a majority of the committed configuration. The manouevre the run needed - cutting the single committed voter off from the majority side as well, so requestVote's existing-leader guard (raft.go:1690-1700) does not refuse the vote - is an ordinary partition shape, and two executions produced the outcome while two settled-schedule executions did not, so the manifestation is schedule dependent while the decision itself is unrepaired by the library.

7da03e78394f41fdad540ae0824ec2a6-gap-1.explanation: The election part is now resolved by a complete comparison: receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 has comparison 0 violated at witness event index 22 (leader with two votes against a committed quorum of three, co-existing with the majority-side leader) and its control holding at index 25. Reproduction depends on whether the single committed voter on the isolated side still hears the majority-side leader, because requestVote refuses candidates while a leader is known (raft.go:1690-1700); with immediate isolation it reproduced twice, with the settled schedule it did not. Entry-level divergence between the two leaders remains unwitnessed, so the gap stays open on that point.

counterevidence: The flag-off controls in both receipts keep the committed configuration and cannot win on the isolated side.
Two settled-schedule executions did not produce the minority win; the difference is explained by whether the isolated partner still heard the majority-side leader, so no frequency claim is made.
The redundant configuration re-checks in the last receipt were incomplete because the two scenarios emit the same restart event name; they carry no new claim and are not used.
limitations: Only the leadership decision and the coexistence with the majority-side leader are observed; no entry-level divergence or lost acknowledged entry is witnessed.
The observed windows are bounded, so no occurrence-rate or absence bound is established.
The scenario restarts the former leader of an enlarged cluster; other roles, change types and chain orders are not explored.
interpretations.joint_history: Receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 supplies the configuration comparison and receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 supplies the election comparison; both are complete executions of the same five-voter scenario over identical stores, sizes and snapshot timing, and both report the same configuration values (index 1 with three servers against expected 14 with five, controls at 14 with five). They are separate complete histories rather than fragments: each built its own cluster, and only the comparison declarations and result event names differ between them.
